readings.core_relation: ConvNeXt combines modern training with a convolutional redesign separating spatial and channel mixing. It exceeds Swin-B's classification accuracy and throughput, demonstrating competitive recognition without attention.
readings.scope: ImageNet-1K training, 384 x 384 inputs, V100; ConvNeXt-B: 85.1% versus 84.5%. ImageNet-22K pretraining yields 87.8% for ConvNeXt-XL. COCO and ADE20K comparisons are competitive; architectural changes use fixed training and approximately controlled computation.
readings.witness: a convolutional route to competitive recognition at both training scales

readings.core_relation: ConvNeXt-B exceeds Swin-B in classification accuracy and throughput with fewer FLOPs, and improves downstream detection and segmentation scores. This supports competitive convolutional features, not highest classification accuracy or demonstrated downstream speed gains.
readings.scope: Classification: ImageNet-1K, 384 x 384, V100. EfficientNetV2-L scores higher at 480 x 480. Downstream: ImageNet-22K pretraining, Cascade Mask R-CNN and UperNet; ADE20K uses 640 x 640 crops and multi-scale testing.
readings.witness: they measure prediction quality rather than the classification speed benefit

readings.core_relation: Increasing optimization from 7,000 to 30,000 iterations improves reconstruction but lowers rendering speed and increases storage. Quality versus Mip-NeRF360 depends on the metric. Restricting gradients to ten Gaussians sharply worsens PSNR and destabilizes optimization.
readings.scope: Mip-NeRF360 dataset: PSNR 25.60 to 27.21 dB, rendering 160 to 134 fps, storage 523 to 734 MB. Gradient ablation uses downsampled Truck, Garden, Bicycle inputs. Weak coverage artifacts and visibility popping persist.
readings.witness: Preserving gradients is therefore consequential in these scenes

readings.core_relation: One tile/depth GPU radix sort supplies shared front-to-back blending lists. Reversing those lists and reconstructing opacity from final accumulations permits gradients for every blended primitive with constant extra per-pixel storage, avoiding individual sorting and contribution histories.
readings.scope: 16 x 16 tiles; blending stops at opacity saturation and shared ordering approximates visibility. L1 plus D-SSIM updates geometry, opacity, and appearance; positional gradients trigger cloning or splitting.

readings.core_relation: ConvNeXt-B improves accuracy and throughput over Swin-B and yields higher COCO box/mask AP. Neutral activation changes, saturated kernel gains, and divergent unnormalized downsampling support the combined design rather than every Transformer convention individually.
readings.scope: Classification: ImageNet-1K, 384 x 384, V100. COCO: ImageNet-22K pretraining, Cascade Mask R-CNN, 3x schedule. GELU alone adds no accuracy; kernels beyond 7 x 7 add no gain; resolution-change normalization is required.
readings.witness: the evidence supports the combined design

readings.core_relation: Adaptive anisotropic Gaussians and a differentiable tile rasterizer retaining all contributing gradients combine interactive novel-view rendering with competitive reconstruction, rather than uniform superiority over radiance-field baselines.
readings.scope: Static scenes initialized from sparse structure-from-motion points; 13 real and bounded synthetic scenes. After 30,000 iterations: 134-154 fps on A6000 at native resolutions, approximately 27-42 minutes training. Mip-NeRF360 retains higher PSNR on its dataset; large storage, poor-coverage artifacts, and blending-order artifacts remain.
readings.witness: Interactive rendering therefore accompanies competitive reconstruction rather than uniform metric superiority

readings.core_relation: Shared tile/depth sorting reduces visibility-processing overhead. Reverse traversal reconstructs intermediate blending quantities from final opacity, avoiding growing per-pixel histories while retaining gradients without a predetermined splat-count cap.
readings.scope: Projected Gaussians occupy overlapping 16 x 16 tiles; one GPU radix sort organizes lists. Shared-memory batches blend front to back until opacity saturation. Large splats make shared ordering approximate; the operation accommodates variable depth complexity.
readings.witness: storage per pixel need not grow with the number of contributing splats

readings.core_relation: Optimizable anisotropic Gaussians, adaptive primitive allocation, and tile rendering with reconstructed backward opacity enable fast scene exploration without limiting gradient contributors. Reconstruction compares favorably on SSIM/LPIPS but not uniformly on PSNR.
readings.scope: Static scenes, sparse structure-from-motion initialization without normal estimation; held-out views across three real-scene datasets. At 30,000 iterations: 134-154 fps on A6000 after approximately 27-42 minutes training. Hundreds of megabytes, weakly observed-region artifacts, and visibility-related popping limit the tradeoff.
readings.witness: higher SSIM and lower LPIPS on all three datasets

readings.core_relation: ConvNeXt transfers design choices into a convolutional backbone under fixed modern training. A narrow-width depthwise kernel precedes channel expansion, supporting higher classification accuracy and throughput than Swin-B without attention.
readings.scope: 7 x 7 kernel, fourfold expansion; ImageNet-1K training at 384 x 384, V100. ImageNet-22K pretraining yields 87.8% for ConvNeXt-XL. COCO/ADE20K results extend competitiveness beyond classification; attention removal is not isolated as the cause.
readings.witness: rather than identifying attention removal as an isolated cause of improvement

readings.core_relation: A 7 x 7 depthwise convolution mixes space before fourfold pointwise expansion and contraction mix channels. This keeps spatial filtering at narrow width while separating spatial from channel processing.
readings.scope: Layer normalization and one GELU within residual blocks; nonoverlapping 4 x 4 stem and normalized separate downsampling. Sequential ImageNet-1K evaluation fixes 300-epoch AdamW training and roughly controls FLOPs; small-regime results average three seeds. Effects are conditional on preceding architecture.
readings.witness: rather than an independent component effect

readings.core_relation: Modern training improves the baseline; GELU substitution alone is neutral, while fewer activations improve accuracy. Normalized separate downsampling enables a roadmap model exceeding Swin-T, and ConvNeXt-B exceeds Swin-B's COCO AP. Findings support coordinated redesign.
readings.scope: Sequential ImageNet-1K changes under fixed training: GELU 80.6%, one activation 81.3%, final model 82.0% versus 81.3%. Downsampling without added normalization diverges. COCO uses ImageNet-22K pretraining, Cascade Mask R-CNN, 3x schedule; component comparisons depend on preceding changes.
readings.witness: Each comparison is conditional on preceding modifications

readings.core_relation: Adaptive anisotropic Gaussians with directional color and a differentiable tile rasterizer enable tractable scene fitting and interactive rendering. Shared depth sorting accelerates approximate blending while retaining unrestricted gradient contributors.
readings.scope: Static scenes initialized from sparse structure-from-motion points; 13 real and bounded synthetic scenes. At 30,000 iterations: 134-154 fps, native resolutions, A6000, roughly 27-42 minutes training. Mip-NeRF360 comparison favors SSIM/LPIPS but not PSNR on its dataset; storage costs, poorly observed-region artifacts, and popping persist.
readings.witness: Interactive rendering is obtained at a substantial storage cost relative to neural radiance fields

readings.core_relation: ConvNeXt separates spatial filtering from channel mixing: a narrow-width 7 x 7 depthwise convolution precedes fourfold pointwise expansion and contraction, widening spatial coverage with fewer spatial-processing channels.
readings.scope: One LayerNorm and GELU per block; normalized stride-two transitions stabilize training. Sequential evaluation fixes a 300-epoch AdamW recipe and roughly controls FLOPs, using three-seed averages in the smaller regime. Unequal intermediate costs and preceding changes limit individual-component attribution.
readings.witness: Holding training fixed distinguishes the architectural trajectory from the initial recipe gain

readings.core_relation: The Gaussian model improves SSIM/LPIPS over Mip-NeRF360 but trails PSNR. Longer optimization improves reconstruction while increasing training time and storage and lowering rendering speed. A ten-splat gradient cap sharply worsens Truck PSNR and destabilizes optimization.
readings.scope: Mip-NeRF360 dataset, 30,000 iterations, A6000: 134 fps and 734 MB versus 8.6 MB. Budget comparison starts at 7,000 iterations. Truck ablation: 24.81 to 13.84 dB. Approximate visibility can cause popping.

readings.core_relation: Gaussian splatting combines fast rendering with better SSIM/LPIPS but lower PSNR than Mip-NeRF360 and much larger storage. Longer fitting improves quality while slowing rendering; Truck's gradient-cap ablation supports retaining all blended contributors.
readings.scope: Mip-NeRF360 dataset, 30,000 iterations: 134 fps on A6000 after 41 minutes 33 seconds, 734 versus 8.6 MB. Tanks & Temples compares 7,000 and 30,000 iterations. Truck PSNR falls from 24.81 to 13.84 dB with ten-splat gradients; coverage artifacts and popping persist.
readings.witness: This supports retaining gradients for all blended contributors in that setting

readings.core_relation: Tile/depth sorting replaces per-pixel sorting; reverse traversal reconstructs blending information from final opacity instead of storing contribution histories. This retains gradients for all contributors and makes splat rendering usable for optimization with varying depth complexity.
readings.scope: 16 x 16 tiles, one GPU radix sort, front-to-back blending until saturation. Losses update geometry, opacity, and spherical harmonic color with gradient-guided cloning and splitting. Shared tile ordering makes blending approximate.
readings.witness: rather than accelerating display through a fixed gradient cutoff

readings.core_relation: ConvNeXt progressively modernizes convolution under an improved fixed training recipe, separating spatial/channel mixing without specialized attention. ConvNeXt-B exceeds Swin-B accuracy with 12.5% higher throughput, supporting convolution as a tested recognition alternative.
readings.scope: ImageNet-1K, 384 x 384, V100: 85.1% versus 84.5%. ImageNet-22K pretraining/fine-tuning yields 87.8% for ConvNeXt-XL. COCO/ADE20K match or exceed evaluated Swin counterparts. Attention's usefulness for multimodal interaction or structured outputs remains unsettled.
readings.witness: without settling attention's usefulness for multimodal interaction or structured outputs

readings.core_relation: Placing the 7 x 7 depthwise convolution before fourfold pointwise expansion keeps spatial mixing at narrow width, reducing its cost while dense layers mix channels. Normalization at separate stage transitions prevents the observed divergence.
readings.scope: Residual blocks retain one GELU and LayerNorm; stride-two transitions add normalization. Sequential ResNet modifications use fixed 300-epoch AdamW training, augmentation, regularization, and roughly controlled FLOPs; small models average three seeds. Results support successive combined designs, not independently isolated component effects.
readings.witness: does not independently isolate every component's effect
